## Now

Closed without a change or done as read, each in full in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md under Items closed,
parked or shortened: 156, the ground's atlas and the anisotropic filter, nothing changing by the
decision of 2026-11-04; 164, the engine's split packages at the restore, read with nothing to
change.

29. **Generation and meshing on the GPU, the blocks kept on the CPU (Decision 12).** Part one, the
    noise fields, landed at `2549786` and `1d31dda` on 2026-10-25, every noise in fixed point and
    the caves' readings in a compute shader read back without a wait, verified bit for bit against
    the CPU path. The meshing moved to the workers at `bb0b9bb` the same day, update.mesh under half
    a millisecond in the flights. Part three went with the far land (Decision 41). Part two, a
    compute mesher a section, is held on its numbers, 1 to 2.6 ms of a frame in flights alone
    against several commits over days, for a decision, Decision 12 being the owner's. The item as it
    stood is in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md under Items closed, parked or shortened. Answered on 2026-11-11 at
    about 16:40, part two stays parked.

203. **The frame of 66 to 75 ms each half minute, read and mended.** Item 202's Reply holds one
    frame of 66 to 75 ms past the 880th of each run, its time in `stage.First` with no system above
    0.06 ms and nothing streamed, taken for the world's save in `Begin` from its place and not from
    a mark. Asked, marks around the save's parts so that the frame is read and not taken for, the
    parts in ms over three runs under the exclusive lock, then the mend, the part that takes the
    time done off the main thread or spread over frames with what is saved unchanged, a save and a
    load of a changed world compared byte for byte or by its hash in a test. The frame's worst
    within a window that holds a save is the reading, before and after. No picture, since nothing
    seen changes.

204. **The sections drawn late inside the drawn reach.** Item 201's Reply counts, of 246 sections
    with faces, 6 deep ones at height 1 held 1.5 s by the reach in three dimensions and 3 hidden
    until a flood 6 s after they entered the reach, not drawn meanwhile. Asked, the two groups read
    first, where each section lies against the eye and what the flood and `Reach.Within` say of it
    frame by frame, and whether a player sees a hole (a capture at the frame one is missing, beside
    the frame it is drawn), then the mend where a hole shows, a section within the drawn reach and
    the eye's sight released by the step's flood or sooner, with a test that holds no visible
    section undrawn past a bound of frames after it enters the reach. The slow frames and the felt
    time of item 202's table held no worse, by the same flight. A picture in the devlog where a hole
    showed.

## Verdicts

No verdict is open. Verdicts 1 to 13 are settled, said under each in REVIEW-ARCHIVE.md.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 The old game is replaced in place, its history kept; 2 The license stays MIT; 3 `e3d`
comes from the engine's checkout; 4 What the game finds the engine lacks goes to the engine's
ASKS.md, as before; 5 Prose is technical and generic; 6 Development resumes; the sky, the shadows
and the icons are the game's week; 7 Nothing in the sky faces the camera; the sun, the moon and the
stars are fixed on the sky and turn with the hour; 8 The mobs' sizes and models may be the other
game's, since they are numbers; 9 The tonemapping is the engine's somewhat boring curve; 10 The
review's files are committed by the batch that comes next, and by the reviewer at most once a day;
11 The list of 2026-10-20 at 23:30, in the reviewer's order; 12 Compute shaders for generation, the
direction of 2026-10-21; 13 The chosen packs set the look, read from the player's copy and never
shipped; 14 A modpack is the reference of the game's feel, read for shapes, numbers and ideas, and
nothing of it ships; 15 The six candidates of Decision 14 are taken; 16 The screen probes stay off
in the game, and the cascades' faults go to the engine; 17 The windows after Recolourful Containers
and the HUD after Bare Bones, read from the player's packs, and the game's own art moved toward
them; 18 The three packs are not shipped and are fetched at first start instead; 19 A screenshot on
F2; 20 Simple Grass Flowers as a fourth default pack, through block state variants; 21 The look the
game aims at is the modpack's gallery; 22 Packs give pictures alone, and every rule is the game's
own; 23 The look without a pack takes Bare Bones' colors; 24 The README's pictures, an animation at
its head and pictures in its parts; 25 Three words during item 46's scouting, the sky's bodies cut,
the rifts in villages and the sun's look; 26 The engine's F1 and F3 come to the game; 27 More

59. **Anisotropic filtering at 16 everywhere.** Decided on 2026-11-04 at 11:07, anisotropic
   filtering is at 16 everywhere, since it is cheap and looks better at steep angles. So every
   sampler that reads a texture, color, normal, surface or atlas, filters anisotropically at 16, or
   at the device's most where it offers less, at every quality and with no knob; the shadow, probe
   and table samplers that are not textures keep their own filters. The game's textures read through
   the engine's samplers, so it comes with the engine's item 201 and the next package; the game sets
   nothing. Added at 11:40, the game is pixel filtering and needs no change, so its atlas stays at
   Point and item 156 is closed.

60. **Version tags.** Decided at about 14:00 on 2026-11-08, after every commit of the Unity
    Essentials repositories was tagged as `v2.0.30` and the like, the three projects take tags too,
    with the review's questions answered at 14:1x. The form is `v6.0.91`, the letter v before
    `build/version.sh`'s number. Tags go on each major or minor change and on the commits packages
    were built from, since a tag on every commit clutters the list and is unnecessary, the tags
    marking releases some time apart with meaningful changes and not commits apart. The major and
    the minor are the sessions' to raise, each session working on the project deciding when the time
    is right to raise the minor or the major, every commit counting as a patch, with full liberty
    once a step is done and meaningful changes were made. N 6.3 holds the rule and the reviewer sets
    the tags as it pushes. `v0.2.0` marks `7e052e8`, which set 0.2 (Decision 57), set at 14:12; a
    release build of `build/publish.sh` is tagged when the owner names one. Decision 57 stands with
    the game's session able to raise the version as well as the reviewer.

    was shown finding the personal name in six files of four repositories, this game's `LICENSE`

    Powerful.exr, a lookup build/unity-lut.py writes from that strip, a gamma of w 0.225, and a

    and on the sessions' knowledge of work in progress, in scenes_sponza explicitly and probably
    everywhere else. The rule from it, in STYLE.md's Register and as N 4.11, is that a comment
    stands on the code's own terms. It says what the code does and why in the engine's words; a
    number taken from elsewhere stands with the reason it is right here, what it makes the frame or
    the program do, and the source is named once in the documents' references and not in the
    comment; the file names of outside assets, another product's profile or process as the

    comment. Item 159 carries STYLE.md's sentence and the game's own sweep.

What else of the game the engine's origin of 264 changes the meaning of, read at `f201940` against
the engine's 6.2.60-local.264.6 (`3768c988`), with no change made. The engine keeps a world-number
twin of each lighting function that takes a point (`lights.slang:750-769`), which takes the origin
off again (`placeOf`), and the `world` of a pixel is its place plus the origin, so every use below
reads as before. With the game's origin on, the world numbers stay under about 5,000 blocks, where a
float's step is a 2,048th of a block, and none of them shows.

- `bits.slang:17` reads the instance's translation, a place since 264, and the settled edit adds
  `modelPush.origin` to it. A second form keeps the place there and sets `middle.place` in place of
  `middle.world` at `bits.slang:44-45`, with no round trip.
- `terrain.slang:275` and `:287` snap the sun's shadow's point to eighths in world numbers
  (`pixelMiddle(input.world, ...)`) and hand it to `lightReaching`, which takes the origin off
  again. `lightReachingPlaced(pixelMiddle(input.place, ...))` snaps to the same eighths, the
  engine's origin being whole blocks, and is the trial that mended the stripes with the game's
  origin off.
- `terrain.slang:176`, `:298`, `:350` and `:356` take the block, the rim and the texture's place
  from world numbers by `floor` and `frac`. The place gives the same values, the origin being whole
  blocks, where `block` and the texture's place change together.
- `terrain.slang:410` calls `mirrored(..., world, ...)`, and `mirroredPlaced(..., place, ...)` takes
  no round trip.
- `terrain.slang:420` reads the haze by the world's height, `world.y`, which stays a world number.
- `mob.slang:27-28` call `arriving` and `lightReaching` with `input.world`, and their `Placed` twins
  take `input.place`. `mob.slang:65` sets `up.world` from `input.base.world`, which setting
  `up.place` from `input.base.place` does without the round trip.
- No game shader reads a matrix of the engine's. `terrain.slang:168` reads the instance's color and
  not its rows, and `cavefields.slang` works in the land's whole columns outside the engine's
  drawing.
- On the CPU, `WaterMirror.cs:43` and `GameCommands.cs:745` and `:773` cast the engine's rays from
  the screen and `Measurements.cs:197`, `:243` and `:263` take its points to the screen, whose
  working 264 changed and the rehearsal read alike with the game's origin on. `HeldLights.cs:66-71`
  and `BlastEffects.cs:104` and `:122` hand the engine world points it places itself.

Nothing beyond the bits' edit changes meaning as the game ships. The `Placed` twins are the forms
that stay exact where a place's numbers are small and a world's are not.

The game's side of the engine's part 7, read on 6.2.60 with the game at `f201940` as it ships, from

What `Recenter` does in its frame (`VoxelGame.cs:546-564`), called from `Begin` (`:645`) before
anything is stepped or drawn. The step is to the multiple of 1,024 nearest the player once it is
4,096 out along x or z (`LandOrigin.cs:84-98`), so a walk or a flight moves the origin 4,096 at once
and a teleport by any multiple of 1,024, and y never moves. In order:

1. `Renderer.Shift` (`ChunkRenderer.cs:952-984`) uploads every section part's mesh again, uploads
   the lamps' cubes again (`MakeLampCubes`, `:679`), gives every part and group a new `Transform`,
   moves the emitters' matrices, marks every group's faces changed and has the lamps gathered again.
2. Every ECS `Body`, the player's and the camera with it, every arrow and every blast moves by the
   step.
3. The mobs' homes and last places (`Mob.cs:193`), the fall's last height (`Vitals.cs:74`), the
   steps' voices (`GameSounds.cs:88`), the blasts' clouds and flashes, set again in the engine by
   `SetParticleEmitterPosition` and `SetLightPosition` (`BlastEffects.cs:112-124`), the bits' bodies
   (`BlockBits.cs:88`) and the rings on the water (`AmbientParticles.cs:137`) move by it.
4. `LandOrigin.MoveTo` last. The held torch's light is set from the hand the next frame, and the sky
   takes no place.

So the engine is handed again every section's mesh as a new one, every part's matrix moved by the
step, the lamps' cubes as new meshes and the camera moved by the step, all in one frame.
